In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the D it of the 3d surface is mainly dominated by the sidewall region, and the corner region only accounts for a small portion.

the D it at the top surface is not the dominant contributor for the high D it of the 3 D surfaces, while the corner regions, which are inevitably formed at the 3D structures and thus are hard to be eliminated by the conventional planar process, are the primary source of the high D it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in addition to the top/side surfaces, the corner regions of 3D surfaces should also be taken into consideration for D it reduction.
the D it at 100 nm wide fins can be reduced to the level of the planar surface by optimizing the forming gas annealing process.
the high D it at the 3D surface is mainly attributed to the high D it in the corner region, which can be effectively reduced by the forming gas annealing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the D it of the 3d surface can be significantly reduced by forming gas annealing.
the D it at 2D planar surfaces can serve as a good indicator to the D it at the 3D surface, and thus the D it of 3D surfaces can be predicted by extrapolating from the 2D counterparts.
the high local D it at the corners can be effectively reduced by optimizing the fin width.
